knowledge_point.title: Evaluating Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S,$$

where $r(u,v)=⟨3u+v,\,3u-v,\,3v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 3.$

*Hint: $‖r_u′\times r_v′‖=3\sqrt{22}.$*

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=3\sqrt{22}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$f(r(u,v))=(3u+v)-(3u-v)=2v.$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as

$$\begin{aligned}\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S&=\iint_D f(r(u,v))‖r_u′\times r_v′‖\,\text{d}A\\&=3\sqrt{22}\iint_D 2v\,\text{d}A\\&=3\sqrt{22}\int_0^{3}2v\,\text{d}v\cdot\int_0^{2}1\,\text{d}u\\&=3\sqrt{22}[v^{2}]_0^{3}[u]_0^{2}\\&=3\sqrt{22}(9-0)(2-0)\\&=54\sqrt{22}.\end{aligned}$$

question.:question/problem:

$$\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S,$$

where $r(u,v)=⟨u+3v,\,u-3v,\,2v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 1.$

*Hint: $‖r_u′\times r_v′‖=2\sqrt{11}.$*

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{11}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$f(r(u,v))=(u+3v)-(u-3v)=6v.$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as

$$\begin{aligned}\iint_S(x-y)\,\text{d}S&=\iint_D f(r(u,v))‖r_u′\times r_v′‖\,\text{d}A\\&=2\sqrt{11}\iint_D 6v\,\text{d}A\\&=2\sqrt{11}\int_0^{1}6v\,\text{d}v\cdot\int_0^{2}1\,\text{d}u\\&=2\sqrt{11}[3v^{2}]_0^{1}[u]_0^{2}\\&=2\sqrt{11}(3-0)(2-0)\\&=12\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(3x-2y+3z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u+v,\,2u+v,\,-v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-\frac{1}{2}\le u\le \frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{2}\le v\le 2\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{2}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{2}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3x-2y+3z)\,{|}_{x=2u+v\,y=2u+v\,z=-v} \\  & =3(2u+v)-2(2u+v)+3(-v) \\  & =2(u-v)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2(u-v)\cdot 2\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =4\sqrt{2}{∬}_{D}\,(u-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & =4\sqrt{2}{\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{2}({\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}u-v\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =4\sqrt{2}{\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{2}{[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}-vu]}_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\text{d}v \\  & =4\sqrt{2}{\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{2}[((-\frac{v}{2})+\frac{1}{8})-(\frac{v}{2}+\frac{1}{8})]\text{d}v \\  & =4\sqrt{2}{\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{2}(0-v)\text{d}v \\  & =4\sqrt{2}{[-\frac{{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{\frac{1}{2}}^{2} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}[((-2))-((-\frac{1}{8}))] \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\cdot (-\frac{15}{8}) \\  & =-\frac{15\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(xy+xz)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,2v,\,6v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le \frac{1}{2},\,0\le v\le 2\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{10}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=2\sqrt{10}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(xy+xz)\,{|}_{x=u\,y=2v\,z=6v} \\  & =(u)(2v)+(u)(6v) \\  & =8uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8uv\cdot 2\sqrt{10}\,\text{d}A \\  & =16\sqrt{10}{∬}_{D}\,uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =16\sqrt{10}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}uv\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & =16\sqrt{10}({\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}u\,\text{d}u)({\int }_{0}^{2}v\,\text{d}v) \\  & =16\sqrt{10}\cdot {[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}\cdot {[\frac{{v}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =16\sqrt{10}[(\frac{1}{8})-(0)]\cdot [(2)-(0)] \\  & =16\sqrt{10}\cdot \frac{1}{8}\cdot 2 \\  & =4\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(x+2y-z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u-v,\,2u+2v,\,2v⟩
$$

 
over the domain $D=\{(u,v)\,:\,\frac{1}{2}\le u\le 1,\,\frac{5}{2}\le v\le 3\}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=6.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=6.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(x+2y-z)\,{|}_{x=u-v\,y=2u+2v\,z=2v} \\  & =(u-v)+2(2u+2v)-(2v) \\  & =5u+v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,(5u+v)\cdot 6\,\text{d}A \\  & =6{∬}_{D}\,(5u+v)\,\text{d}A \\  & =6{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}({\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}(5u+v)\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =6{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}{[\frac{5{u}^{2}}{2}+vu]}_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}\text{d}v \\  & =6{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}[(v+\frac{5}{2})-(\frac{v}{2}+\frac{5}{8})]\text{d}v \\  & =6{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}(\frac{15}{8}+\frac{v}{2})\text{d}v \\  & =6{[\frac{15v}{8}+\frac{{v}^{2}}{4}]}_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3} \\  & =6[(\frac{45}{8}+\frac{9}{4})-(\frac{75}{16}+\frac{25}{16})] \\  & =6[\frac{45}{8}+\frac{9}{4}-(\frac{75}{16}+\frac{25}{16})] \\  & =\frac{39}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
A shell is parametrized by $r(x,\theta)=⟨x,2x^2\cos\theta,2x^2\sin\theta⟩$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le\theta<2\pi$. Its charge density is $d(x,y,z)=\frac{x(y^2+z^2)}{\sqrt{16x^2+1}}$, and $‖r_x′\times r_\theta′‖=2x^2\sqrt{16x^2+1}$. Evaluate $Q=\iint_S d\,\text{d}S$.

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\,\text{d}A.
$$

Previously, we determined that our surface can be parametrized as

$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [0,2],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ),
$$

and the norm of the fundamental vector product is

$$
‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖=2{x}^{2}\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(x,\theta )$ into $d(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}d(r(x,\theta )) & =\frac{x({y}^{2}+{z}^{2})}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{x((2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2})}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}d(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}d(r(x,\theta ))‖{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\frac{4{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}}\cdot 2{x}^{2}\sqrt{16{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{x}^{7}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =[{x}^{8}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [\theta ]_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =(256-0)\cdot (2\pi -0) \\  & =512\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=2u,\,y=-3v,\,z=4v
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u,\,-3v,\,4v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-3,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-8,\,-6⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =x(y+z)\,{|}_{x=2u\,y=-3v\,z=4v} \\  & =2u(-3v+4v) \\  & =2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le \frac{1}{2}\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}x(y+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2uv\cdot 10\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =5\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =5[(1)-(0)]\cdot [(\frac{1}{4})-(0)] \\  & =5\cdot 1\cdot \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=6-3u-2v
$$

for $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le 1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,6-3u-2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(6-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3,\,2,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =4xy\,{|}_{x=u\,y=v\,z=6-3u-2v} \\  & =4uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 1\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}4xy\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4uv\sqrt{14}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{∬}_{D}\,4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{14}{\int }_{0}^{2}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot [{u}^{2}]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\sqrt{14}[(4)-(0)]\cdot [(1)-(0)] \\  & =\sqrt{14}\cdot 4\cdot 1 \\  & =4\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v,\,y=u-v,\,z=0
$$

for $\frac{1}{2}\le u\le 1$ and $\frac{5}{2}\le v\le 3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u-v,\,0⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,0,\,-2⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+0+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =xy+z\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u-v\,z=0} \\  & =(u+v)(u-v) \\  & ={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,\frac{1}{2}\le u\le 1,\,\frac{5}{2}\le v\le 3\},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}(xy+z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}({\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}-{v}^{2}u]}_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}[((-v^{2})+\frac{1}{3})-((-\frac{v^{2}}{2})+\frac{1}{24})]\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3}(\frac{7}{24}-\frac{{v}^{2}}{2})\text{d}v \\  & =2{[\frac{7v}{24}-\frac{{v}^{3}}{6}]}_{\frac{5}{2}}^{3} \\  & =2[(\frac{7}{8}+(-\frac{9}{2}))-(\frac{35}{48}+(-\frac{125}{48}))] \\  & =2[\frac{7}{8}-\frac{9}{2}-(\frac{35}{48}-\frac{125}{48})] \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

and

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-2yz\,\text{d}S,
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
x=u+v,\,y=u,\,z=v
$$

for $-\frac{1}{2}\le u\le \frac{1}{2}$ and $-\frac{5}{2}\le v\le -\frac{1}{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,u,\,v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & ={x}^{2}-2yz\,{|}_{x=u+v\,y=u\,z=v} \\  & =(u+v)^{2}-2uv \\  & ={u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if we denote 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-\frac{1}{2}\le u\le \frac{1}{2\},\,-\frac{5}{2}\le v\le -\frac{1}{2}},
$$

our surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}{x}^{2}-2yz\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,({u}^{2}+{v}^{2})\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\,{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}({\int }_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}u)\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}{[\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}+u{v}^{2}]}_{u=-\frac{1}{2}}^{u=\frac{1}{2}}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}[(\frac{v^{2}}{2}+\frac{1}{24})-((-\frac{v^{2}}{2})+(-\frac{1}{24}))]\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\frac{1}{12}+{v}^{2}\,\text{d}v \\  & =\sqrt{3}{[\frac{1}{12}v+\frac{1}{3}{v}^{3}]}_{-\frac{5}{2}}^{-\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}[((-\frac{1}{24})+(-\frac{1}{24}))-((-\frac{5}{24})+(-\frac{125}{24}))] \\  & =\sqrt{3}(-\frac{1}{24}-\frac{1}{24})-\sqrt{3}(-\frac{5}{24}-\frac{125}{24}) \\  & =\frac{16\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
